title: Scrum - Project Management Plan
text:
You can find our scrum trello board here.



After creating the product backlog for the game, we extracted the most essential features of the minimum viable product version of the game to focus on in the first sprint. These product backlog items were then broken up into smaller, more specific tasks for the sprint backlog. All sprint backlog tasks were also tagged & color coded by team/responsibility (e.g. design, programming, art & audio, UI/UX design, etc.). Additionally, we created user stories from the product backlog items to help organize the team and enhance our understanding of the sprint goals.
Here is an image of the labels and their colours in the trello board. 



The burndown chart for the sprint tracks the sprint backlog items, ranked by priority, and the progress to completion based on the estimated time requirement.
Access the burdown chart spreadsheet here. The charts can be viewed in seperate pages which you can navigate through at the bottom.

title: Brainstorm
text:
We conducted a brainstorming session to come up ideas for our game.
In the meeting we focussed on these important details:

Core Concepts
Unique Selling Points
Story and Environment
Places & People in the Game
Gameplay & Rules
Progression
Goals
Artstyle
Name

Our session consisted of two parts:
1: Come up with as many ideas as possible in each category
2: Discard any ideas that did not fit with our game concept
By doing this, we could throw as many ideas as possible at the board and come back later to see what worked and what didn’t.


You can find our brainstorming trello board here.



We (Aimee Kelly and Beckett Brooks) conducted our brainstorming session on Wednesday, the 30th of September. This session lasted 2 hours (with a break in between) during our 2 hour break from classes in SETU.
